changed.title: The Godsil-Gutman signed determinant estimator for real entry weights (known result rebuilt)
changed.statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ),
  let signed : (Fin n × Fin n → Bool) → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ := fun s =>
    fun i j => if s (i,j) then -A i j else A i j
  let weights : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ := fun row col => A row col ^ 2
  (∑ s : Fin n × Fin n → Bool, (Matrix.det (signed s)) ^ 2) =
    (2 : ℝ)^(n*n) * weights.permanent
changed.unlocks: Gives an unbiased determinant estimator of weighted perfect matching counts.
changed.context: Expand the determinant squared as a sum over pairs of permutations. Two distinct permutations use some matrix cell exactly once between them. Flipping only its sign pairs the terms with opposite sign for that pair. Equal permutations have sign squared one and give the product of squared entries once for every sign matrix. Summing these diagonal terms yields the permanent. Zero entries and the empty matrix require no exception.
changed.sketch: Expand the determinant squared as a sum over pairs of permutations. Two distinct permutations use some matrix cell exactly once between them. Flipping only its sign pairs the terms with opposite sign for that pair. Equal permutations have sign squared one and give the product of squared entries once for every sign matrix. Summing these diagonal terms yields the permanent. Zero entries and the empty matrix require no exception.

changed.title: A terminal vector of exact window counts recovers every oriented switch at every preceding layer
changed.statement:
∀ (w t : Nat), 0 < w →
  let D := 2^w
  let Rows := Nat → Nat → Bool
  let mass := fun (rows : Rows) (h seed tail : Nat) =>
    ((List.range (2^(w+h))).filter (fun bits =>
      bits % D == seed && (bits >>> h) % D == tail &&
      (List.range h).all (fun i => rows i ((bits >>> i) % (2*D))))).length
  let H := D/2
  let undo := fun (v : Nat → Nat) (j : Nat) =>
    let x := v (j/2)
    let y := v (j/2+H)
    if j%2 = 0 then (if x < y then x else x-y)
    else (if x < y then y-x else y)
  ∀ flags : Nat → Nat → Bool,
    let table : Rows := fun site pattern =>
      let old := pattern%2
      let newBit := (pattern/D)%2
      decide (site < w) || (old == newBit) ||
        ((old == 1) == flags (site-w) ((pattern%D)/2))
    let last := fun z : Nat => mass table (w+t) 0 z
    let back : Nat → Nat → Nat := fun steps =>
      Nat.rec (motive := fun _ => Nat → Nat) last (fun _ prev => undo prev) steps
    (∀ s z : Fin D, mass table (w+t) s.val z.val = last z.val ∧
      1 ≤ last z.val ∧ last z.val ≤ 2^t) ∧
    (∀ j : Fin D, back t j.val = 1) ∧
    ∀ (i : Fin t) (u : Fin H),
      let v : Nat → Nat := back (t-1-i.val)
      Nat.blt (v (u.val+H)) (v u.val) = flags i.val u.val
changed.unlocks: recovers each prefix switch from one positive vector of terminal counts
changed.context: After w free shifts each seed reaches every terminal window once. At a switch the two entries a,b at 2u,2u+1 produce (a,a+b) or (a+b,b) at u,u+D/2. Both inputs are positive, so comparison recovers the orientation and subtraction recovers both inputs. Undo all suffix pairs together, in reverse row order. Positivity persists and the maximum at most doubles at each row.
changed.sketch: After w free shifts each seed reaches every terminal window once. At a switch the two entries a,b at 2u,2u+1 produce (a,a+b) or (a+b,b) at u,u+D/2. Both inputs are positive, so comparison recovers the orientation and subtraction recovers both inputs. Undo all suffix pairs together, in reverse row order. Positivity persists and the maximum at most doubles at each row.

changed.title: The maximum dimension of an affine restriction of a quadratic Boolean function (known result rebuilt)
changed.statement:
∀ n : ℕ,
  let V := Fin n → ZMod 2
  ∀ (f : V → ZMod 2) (M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod 2)),
    (∀ x y : V, f (x+y) + f x + f y + f 0 = dotProduct x (M.mulVec y)) →
    ∀ d : ℕ, (∃ (U : Submodule (ZMod 2) V) (p a : V) (b : ZMod 2),
        d ≤ Module.finrank (ZMod 2) U ∧
        ∀ x ∈ U, f (p+x) = dotProduct a (p+x) + b) ↔ 2*d + M.rank ≤ 2*n
changed.unlocks: Supplies the maximal dimension used in the lower bound in L-lib-506.
changed.context: The maximal affine flat follows from the symplectic decomposition in Mirwald and Schnorr (1992). Prove the dimension and attainment. Estimated proof time 2 to 4 hours after 484.
changed.sketch: On paper. On a translate of U the restriction is affine precisely when the polar form vanishes on U times U. In the quotient by the radical a totally isotropic subspace has dimension at most half the nondegenerate dimension. Add back the radical. The span of that radical and one vector from each hyperbolic pair attains the bound. Extend the restricted affine form to the ambient space.

changed.title: Known result rebuilt: the finite translate-cover argument in the Sipser, Gacs and Lautemann containment
changed.statement:
∀ (n t : Nat) (S : Finset (Fin n → ZMod 2)),
  let Q := 2^n
  let covers := fun (shifts : Fin t → (Fin n → ZMod 2)) =>
    ∀ x : Fin n → ZMod 2, ∃ j : Fin t, x + shifts j ∈ S
  (Q*(Q-S.card)^t < Q^t → ∃ shifts, covers shifts) ∧
  (t*S.card < Q → ∀ shifts, ¬ covers shifts)
changed.unlocks: Supplies the finite completeness and soundness implications of the translate-cover simulation.
changed.context: For each point there are (Q-|S|)^t ordered shift lists missing it because translation is bijective in every coordinate of the list. Sum over Q points and compare with all Q^t lists. In the sparse case the union of the t translates has at most t|S| elements for every list. The two strict comparisons handle t=0. Size 1 to 2 hours.
changed.sketch: For each point there are (Q-|S|)^t ordered shift lists missing it because translation is bijective in every coordinate of the list. Sum over Q points and compare with all Q^t lists. In the sparse case the union of the t translates has at most t|S| elements for every list. The two strict comparisons handle t=0. Size 1 to 2 hours.

changed.title: Finite alteration bound for q-ary covering codes in the derandomization of local SAT search (known result rebuilt)
changed.statement:
∀ (q n r t : Nat), 2 ≤ q → r ≤ n →
  let Word := Fin n → Fin q
  let dist := fun (x y : Word) =>
    ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).filter (fun i => x i ≠ y i)).card
  let A := q^n
  let V := ((List.range (r+1)).map (fun j => Nat.choose n j * (q-1)^j)).sum
  ∃ C : Finset Word, (∀ point : Word, ∃ c ∈ C, dist point c ≤ r) ∧
    C.card * A^t ≤ t*A^t + A*(A-V)^t
changed.unlocks: Provides the finite covering codes for grouped flips and for selecting starting assignments.
changed.context: A radius-r ball contains the sum of choose(n,j)(q-1)^j over j at most r. Among all A^t center lists, exactly (A-V)^t lists miss a fixed word. Double-count missed word and list pairs and select a list no worse than the average. Add each missed word as its own center, and discard repetitions.
changed.sketch: A radius-r ball contains the sum of choose(n,j)(q-1)^j over j at most r. Among all A^t center lists, exactly (A-V)^t lists miss a fixed word. Double-count missed word and list pairs and select a list no worse than the average. Add each missed word as its own center, and discard repetitions.

changed.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 8 ∧ ∀ i j : Fin 6, C.eval (List.ofFn fun k : Fin 6 => decide (k = i ∨ k = j)) = (118589 : ℕ).testBit (6 * min i.val j.val + max i.val j.val)
